theorems.name: valid_name_no_traversal
theorems.doc: **Security (S): no path traversal.** Every filename the gate accepts is a non-empty, ≤64-byte component that is neither `.` nor `..` and contains no path separator or NUL. Appending it after `/armory/` therefore names a direct child of the armory directory: the device can never be steered to a file outside `/armory`. Falsified by `drop_slash_check` (a `/`/`\` could pass) and `drop_dotdot_check` (`..` could pass).
theorems.statement:
theorem valid_name_no_traversal (nm : Slice Std.U8) (h : valid_name nm = ok true) :
    Spec.SafeNameAt nm.val nm.val.length
theorems.proof:
theorem valid_name_no_traversal (nm : Slice Std.U8) (h : valid_name nm = ok true) :
    Spec.SafeNameAt nm.val nm.val.length := by
  unfold valid_name at h
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hpost⟩ := (WP.spec_equiv_exists _ _).1 (valid_name_prefix_facts nm (Slice.len nm))
  rw [hr] at h
  simp only [Result.ok.injEq] at h
  subst h
  simpa [Slice.len_val] using hpost rfl

theorems.name: decode_filename_confined
theorems.doc: **Security (S): decode-then-validate confinement.** Even after percent-decoding, any filename `decode_filename` accepts satisfies the confinement policy on the decoded bytes. This is what makes `%2e%2e` (`..`) and `%2f` (`/`) harmless: they are decoded first and then rejected. Falsified by `validate_before_decode` (validating the raw, still-encoded bytes would accept a decoded `..`).
theorems.statement:
theorem decode_filename_confined (raw out out' : Slice Std.U8) (n : Std.Usize)
    (h : decode_filename raw out = ok (some n, out')) :
    Spec.SafeNameAt out'.val n.val
theorems.proof:
theorem decode_filename_confined (raw out out' : Slice Std.U8) (n : Std.Usize)
    (h : decode_filename raw out = ok (some n, out')) :
    Spec.SafeNameAt out'.val n.val := by
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hpost⟩ := (WP.spec_equiv_exists _ _).1 (decode_filename_wp raw out)
  rw [hr] at h
  simp only [Result.ok.injEq] at h
  exact hpost n out' h

theorems.name: dispatch_pending_goes_to_parser

    (h : pending bytes = ok true) : dispatch bytes = ok Class.Other := by
  unfold dispatch preflight_ready
  simp [h]

theorems.name: decode_filename_ascii
theorems.doc: **S (U5 fix).** Every byte of a name `decode_filename` accepts is ASCII, so building the LittleFS path from it cannot fail: upstream's `StorageManager::with_path` unwraps that conversion, and a DELETE of `%e2%82%ac` (a valid UTF-8, non-ASCII name) panicked the device.
theorems.statement:
theorem decode_filename_ascii (raw out out' : Slice Std.U8) (n : Std.Usize)
    (h : decode_filename raw out = ok (some n, out')) :
    ∀ k, k < n.val → (out'.val[k]!).val < 128
theorems.proof:
theorem decode_filename_ascii (raw out out' : Slice Std.U8) (n : Std.Usize)
    (h : decode_filename raw out = ok (some n, out')) :
    ∀ k, k < n.val → (out'.val[k]!).val < 128 := by
  have hs := Properties.decode_filename_confined raw out out' n h
  intro k hk
  have := hs.2.2.2.2.2 k hk
  simp only [PicoBit.Spec.IsSep, not_or] at this
  omega

theorems.name: mutation_needs_post_or_delete
theorems.doc: **S.** Whatever the port dispatches to a state-changing handler (upload, delete, payload save or run, keyboard target) came with a `POST ` or `DELETE ` method: no GET/HEAD (a link, an image tag, a prefetch) changes the device.
theorems.statement:
theorem mutation_needs_post_or_delete (bytes : Slice Std.U8) (c : Class)
    (h : dispatch bytes = ok c) (hm : is_mutating c = ok true) :
    MethodIs bytes POST ∨ MethodIs bytes DELETE
theorems.proof:
theorem mutation_needs_post_or_delete (bytes : Slice Std.U8) (c : Class)
    (h : dispatch bytes = ok c) (hm : is_mutating c = ok true) :
    MethodIs bytes POST ∨ MethodIs bytes DELETE := by
  rw [is_mutating_iff] at hm
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hpost⟩ := (WP.spec_equiv_exists _ _).1 (dispatch_mut_spec bytes)
  rw [hr] at h
  simp only [Result.ok.injEq] at h
  subst h
  exact hpost hm

theorems.name: delete_never_payload_dd
theorems.doc: **S.** A DELETE that the kernel lets through (`Erase`) never names `payload.dd`, the editor's file (upstream answers 403 for it).
theorems.statement:
theorem delete_never_payload_dd (buf : Slice Std.U8) (len : Std.Usize)
    (h : delete_action buf len = ok DeleteAction.Erase) :
    ¬ (len.val = PAYLOAD_DD.val.length ∧ len.val ≤ buf.val.length ∧
        ∀ k, k < len.val → buf.val[k]! = PAYLOAD_DD.val[k]!)
theorems.proof:
theorem delete_never_payload_dd (buf : Slice Std.U8) (len : Std.Usize)
    (h : delete_action buf len = ok DeleteAction.Erase) :
    ¬ (len.val = PAYLOAD_DD.val.length ∧ len.val ≤ buf.val.length ∧
        ∀ k, k < len.val → buf.val[k]! = PAYLOAD_DD.val[k]!) := by
  have hw := name_is_spec buf PAYLOAD_DD len
  unfold delete_action at h
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hpost⟩ := (WP.spec_equiv_exists _ _).1 hw
  rw [hr] at h
  cases r <;> simp_all

is_dot_name.lean:
def is_dot_name (buf : Slice Std.U8) (len : Std.Usize) : Result Bool := do
  let i := Slice.len buf
  if i < len
  then ok false
  else
    if len = 1#usize
    then let i1 ← Slice.index_usize buf 0#usize
         ok (i1 = DOT)
    else
      if len = 2#usize
      then
        let i1 ← Slice.index_usize buf 0#usize
        if i1 = DOT
        then let i2 ← Slice.index_usize buf 1#usize
             ok (i2 = DOT)
        else ok false
      else ok false
